newsitem.title: USA: No talk Mexico-style aid package for Thailand--IMF.
newsitem.headline: No talk Mexico-style aid package for Thailand--IMF.

text.p: Teams from the IMF are looking at the situation in Thailand after the currency crisis, but there has been no talk of a Mexico-style financial package there, a senior IMF official said on Tuesday.
Asked about such a package after a luncheon speech, IMF first deputy managing director Stanley Fischer said: "They have not discussed that with us."

Asked about the situation in the Philippines after the Thai crisis, Fischer told reporters there had been some reaction on local financial markets, but he added: "The Philippines has handled it very well."
The Philippines has sharply increased interest rates and intervened heavily in the currency market to protect the peso against speculative selling after the Thai baht crisis.
Fischer said it was not yet clear if supplementary measures would be needed in Thailand after the currency crash, but said some were being considered.

"They are thinking of putting in place measures to help firms which could be adversely affected by the change in the exchange rate," he said. He added: "We do not know the extent (of the problem), but if there was a big problem then, as in Mexico you might have to take measures like that."
